title: Ya Sin. Two letters, then listen.
subtitle: The opening letters of the heart of the Quran
then: Ya Sin begins with two separate letters. Ibn Kathir refers back to his discussion at the start of al-Baqarah; {idea}their meaning is known to Allah.{/idea} The Prophet ﷺ said {reward}whoever recites Ya Sin at night seeking Allah's Face will be forgiven.{/reward}
now: You have heard Ya Sin recited at funerals and on Thursday nights, often while your mind was elsewhere. {idea}These two letters are a knock at the door.{/idea} Before the next verse, put the phone face down.
old: I know Ya Sin, I have heard it a hundred times.
new: Its first letters ask me to stop and listen as if for the first time.
try: Recite or listen to Ya Sin once this week at night, seeking only Allah's Face.

title: Sworn by the Quran that is full of wisdom.
subtitle: An oath by the Book itself
then: Allah swears by the Quran itself. Ibn Kathir explains its wisdom means it is {idea}perfect, and falsehood cannot come to it from before or behind.{/idea} The oath prepares the listener for what it confirms: the Prophet ﷺ is truly a messenger.
now: You fact-check every headline and forward that a video is fake. {idea}Here is the one text that falsehood cannot touch.{/idea} {reward}Its wisdom is there for anyone who sits with it.{/reward}
old: The Quran is old and hard to relate to.
new: It is full of wisdom, untouched by falsehood, and speaks to my life now.
try: Read one verse today with its translation and write down one thing it tells you.

title: You are truly one of the messengers.
subtitle: What the oath confirms
then: The surah was revealed while Quraysh met the Prophet ﷺ with {trap}ridicule and mockery.{/trap} Allah answers by oath: {idea}you, O Muhammad ﷺ, are one of the messengers.{/idea} Maududi notes he faced hardship for this message with no selfish motive.
now: When people online mock the Prophet ﷺ, you feel shaken or defensive. {idea}Allah Himself swore to his truth.{/idea} Your job is not to win the comment war but to follow him well.
old: I need others to agree before I feel sure of my faith.
new: Allah has sworn to the truth of His Messenger ﷺ. That settles it for me.
try: Send salawat on the Prophet ﷺ ten times today and learn one of his habits to follow.

title: On a straight path.
subtitle: The way he brought is upright
then: Ibn Kathir says the Prophet ﷺ was {idea}following a straight method, religion, and upright law.{/idea} He links it to the verse saying he guides to {reward}the path of Allah, to whom all matters return.{/reward}
now: Every month a new self-help method, a new routine, a new guru. {trap}You keep zigzagging.{/trap} {idea}The straight path is not new or complicated.{/idea} It is the one he walked.
old: I need to find my own way through trial and error.
new: The straight path has already been walked and shown. I can follow it.
try: Pick one sunnah habit, such as saying bismillah before eating, and keep it all day.

title: Sent down by the Mighty, the Merciful.
subtitle: Who the revelation comes from
then: Ibn Kathir explains the path the Prophet ﷺ brought {idea}is a revelation from the Lord of might{/idea} who is {reward}Most Merciful to His believing servants.{/reward} The listeners in Makkah heard both: power to warn, mercy to invite.
now: Some people grew up hearing only about punishment, others only about mercy. {idea}This verse holds both names in one breath.{/idea} {reward}The rules come from someone who cares about you.{/reward}
old: Religion is either strict and scary, or soft and easy.
new: The One who sent it is both Mighty and Merciful. I can respect Him and trust Him.
try: In your next dua, call on Allah as Al-Aziz and Ar-Rahim together.

title: Their fathers were not warned, so they drifted unaware.
subtitle: Why the Messenger was sent to them
then: Ibn Kathir says this refers to the Arabs, to whom {trap}no warner had come before him.{/trap} He adds that mentioning them does not exclude others, for {idea}the Prophet's mission ﷺ is to all mankind.{/idea}
now: Maybe your parents did not pray, and you grew up without anyone teaching you much. {trap}That is how drift starts.{/trap} {reward}But now the warner has reached you.{/reward} Your story can start differently.
old: My upbringing explains why I am the way I am.
new: Whatever I inherited, the message has now reached me. I can start fresh.
try: Learn one small thing about your faith today that no one ever taught you.

title: The word came true for most of them.
subtitle: Some hearts had already decided
then: Ibn Jarir explains that {trap}punishment became certain for most of them{/trap}, as Allah had decreed they would not believe. The verse prepared the Prophet ﷺ for the reality that {idea}most of his people would refuse.{/idea}
now: Your friends, your office, your feed all say faith is outdated. {trap}It feels like the majority must know something.{/trap} {idea}This verse says plainly that most can be wrong.{/idea} You do not need a crowd.
old: If most people around me do not believe, maybe I am the odd one.
new: Truth is not decided by numbers. Most refused even in the Prophet's time.
try: Ask Allah today: make me among the few who believe and hold firm.

title: Collars to the chin, heads forced up.
subtitle: A picture of being locked away from good
then: Ibn Kathir explains this as a picture of those who refused guidance: {trap}hands tied to their necks so they cannot stretch them to do good.{/trap} Ikrimah reported that Abu Jahl threatened the Prophet ﷺ, and this passage came down about that.
now: Pride works like that collar. Your chin goes up, and you cannot bend to apologize, or reach out to help. {idea}Check where your hands are stuck.{/idea} {reward}A lowered head can still reach out.{/reward}
old: Pride just means I have self-respect.
new: Pride can lock my hands away from doing good. Humility frees them.
try: Reach out today to someone you have been too proud to call first.

title: A wall in front, a wall behind.
subtitle: Barriers between them and the truth
then: Mujahid said the barrier is {trap}between them and the truth{/trap}, leaving them confused. Qatadah said {trap}they move from one misguidance to another.{/trap} Ikrimah reported they would say, there is Muhammad ﷺ, and Abu Jahl could not see him.
now: You keep looping between the same distractions: one app, the next, back to the first. {trap}It feels like walls on every side.{/trap} {idea}Ask Allah to lift the barrier before it hardens.{/idea}
old: I will see the truth whenever I am ready to look.
new: Barriers can build up until I cannot see. I should ask for sight while I still can.
try: Say this dua today: O Allah, remove every barrier between me and the truth.

title: Warned or not, it is the same to them.
subtitle: When reminders stop landing
then: Ibn Kathir says Allah had decreed their misguidance, so {trap}warning them did not help or have any effect.{/trap} He links it to the start of al-Baqarah. For the Prophet ﷺ, it was a reason {idea}not to blame himself.{/idea}
now: You hear a sermon on Friday about backbiting, nod along, and backbite on Saturday. {trap}Same as if you never heard it.{/trap} {idea}The verse is a mirror: do reminders still change you?{/idea}
old: I hear reminders all the time, so I am doing fine.
new: Hearing is not enough. A living heart lets the reminder change something.
try: Take one reminder you heard this week and act on it today in one small way.

title: The warning helps the one who fears Him unseen.
subtitle: Good news of forgiveness and a noble reward
then: After the hardened hearts come those who listen. Ibn Kathir says they fear Allah {idea}even when no one sees them except Allah{/idea}, knowing He watches. {reward}Give them good news of forgiveness and a vast, beautiful reward.{/reward}
now: Alone in your room, browser open, nobody will ever know. {idea}That moment is where this verse lives.{/idea} {reward}Choosing well there is what earns the good news.{/reward}
old: What I do in private does not really count.
new: What I do when only Allah sees is where my faith is proven.
try: In one private moment today, choose the better option because Allah is watching.

title: Your deeds and the footprints you leave behind are written.
subtitle: What you send ahead and what keeps going after you
then: Ibn Kathir says traces means {idea}the legacy they left behind.{/idea} The Prophet ﷺ said whoever starts a good practice gets its reward and that of all who follow it. And {reward}a person's deeds end at death except beneficial knowledge, a righteous child, or ongoing charity.{/reward}
now: The recipe you taught your niece, the habit of prayer your kid picked up from you, the water fountain you chipped in for. {reward}Those keep writing after you are gone.{/reward} {trap}So does the bad habit you made normal.{/trap}
old: My record closes when I die.
new: What others continue from me keeps being written. I can choose what that is.
try: Start one small thing today that could outlast you, like teaching someone a dua.

title: Tell them the story of the town.
subtitle: A parable set before the people of Makkah
then: Allah tells the Prophet ﷺ to set an example before his people who denied him. Ibn Ishaq relayed reports that the town was Antioch, but {idea}some scholars were not sure of that.{/idea} The point is the pattern: {trap}messengers came, and the town had to choose.{/trap}
now: You hear a story in a talk and immediately think of someone else who needs it. {idea}The Quran tells stories so you will see yourself in them.{/idea} Read this one as if it is about your street.
old: Quran stories are about people long ago.
new: Each story is a mirror held up to me and my choices today.
try: As you read the next few verses, ask at each step: which person am I here?

title: Two were denied, so a third was sent.
subtitle: Allah reinforced His messengers
then: Ibn Kathir says the town {trap}hastened to disbelieve in the two{/trap}, so Allah {reward}supported and strengthened them with a third.{/reward} Together they said they were sent from the Lord who created them, calling to worship Him alone.
now: You tried to start a study circle with a friend and nobody came. {idea}Rejection was not the end of the messengers' work.{/idea} {reward}Sometimes Allah sends a third person just when you need one.{/reward}
old: If my good effort is rejected, it was a mistake to try.
new: Allah supports those who keep calling to good. Help can arrive after rejection.
try: Message one friend today and invite them to join you in one good deed.

title: You are only human like us.
subtitle: The oldest excuse for rejecting messengers
then: Ibn Kathir says they reasoned: {trap}we are human and you are human, so why would you get revelation and not us?{/trap} Many nations said the same, he notes, citing verses where people asked {trap}shall mere men guide us?{/trap}
now: Your cousin gives you good advice, and your first thought is: who is he to tell me, he messes up too. {trap}Dismissing the message because of the messenger is an old trick.{/trap} {idea}Weigh the words, not just the person.{/idea}
old: I only take advice from people who are better than me.
new: Truth can come through ordinary people. I should judge the message, not dismiss the messenger.
try: Think of one piece of good advice you rejected because of who said it. Try it today.

title: Our Lord knows we were sent to you.
subtitle: When you cannot prove it, Allah is your witness
then: Ibn Kathir explains their reply: {idea}Allah knows we are His messengers.{/idea} If they were lying, He would have taken vengeance on them, but {reward}He would make them prevail{/reward}, and everyone would learn whose end was good.
now: Someone at work accuses you of something you did not do, and you cannot prove it. {idea}You can still say: Allah knows.{/idea} {reward}That is not weakness. It is the strongest witness there is.{/reward}
old: If I cannot prove I am right, I have lost.
new: Allah knows the truth. His knowledge is enough for me.
try: If you feel misjudged today, say quietly: Allah knows, and leave it there.

title: Our only duty is to convey it clearly.
subtitle: The messengers knew the limits of their job
then: Ibn Kathir explains: {idea}all we have to do is convey the message.{/idea} If you obey, {reward}happiness in this world and the next{/reward} is yours. If not, you will soon know the consequences.
now: You keep rewriting the message to your sibling, trying to get it perfect so they will finally listen. {idea}Be clear, be kind, then let it go.{/idea} The response is not your burden.
old: If they do not accept it, I explained it badly.
new: My duty is clear delivery. Acceptance is between them and Allah.
try: Say one clear, kind thing today that you have been holding back, then stop pushing.

title: You are bad luck for us.
subtitle: Blaming the reminder for the trouble
then: Qatadah said they claimed {trap}if something bad befalls us, it will be because of you.{/trap} Mujahid said they believed people like these messengers always brought punishment on a town. Then came {trap}the threat to stone them.{/trap}
now: Since that friend started reminding you to pray, you feel uncomfortable around them. {trap}You start avoiding them as if they bring bad vibes.{/trap} {idea}The discomfort may be your conscience waking up.{/idea}
old: Since that person came along, things feel worse. They must be the problem.
new: The reminder is not the bad luck. Sometimes discomfort is the start of change.
try: Thank, instead of avoid, the next person who reminds you of Allah.

title: Your bad omen is with you.
subtitle: Because you were reminded? No, you went too far
then: The messengers answered: {trap}your omens are thrown back at you.{/trap} Qatadah said it means, {idea}because we reminded you about Allah, you saw an evil omen in us{/idea}, but in truth they were a people who went beyond limits.
now: Every bad week you blame the boss, the traffic, the economy. {idea}The verse asks you to look at what you carry with you.{/idea} {reward}That is good news: it means you can change something.{/reward}
old: My problems are always caused by other people.
new: Some of my trouble travels with me. Owning it is the first step to fixing it.
try: Tonight, write one problem from today and one way you may have contributed to it.

title: A man came running from the far end of town.
subtitle: One ordinary believer stood up for the messengers

row.title: anyone
sub: even from the edge of town

then: Ibn Ishaq's reports say when the town resolved to kill the messengers, a man came running to help them. {idea}They said his name was Habib, a rope worker{/idea}, sickly, yet {reward}giving half his earnings in charity.{/reward}
now: Someone in the family group chat is being mocked for wearing hijab or for praying, and everyone stays silent. {idea}You are not the imam. You are not important.{/idea} {reward}You can still be the one who comes running.{/reward}
old: Speaking up is for people with status. I am nobody.
new: One ordinary person from the edge of town can stand up for the truth.
try: The next time someone is mocked for their faith, say one supportive sentence.

title: Follow those who ask you for nothing.
subtitle: Two signs of a trustworthy guide
then: The man gave his people two simple reasons. Ibn Kathir says the messengers {reward}asked no wages for the message{/reward} and {idea}were rightly guided in calling to the worship of Allah alone.{/idea}
now: Your feed is full of people who want something from you: a subscription, a click, a donation link. {idea}Notice who gives you good and asks nothing back.{/idea} That is a sign worth trusting.
old: The most popular voice is the one worth following.
new: A guide who wants nothing from me and points to Allah is worth listening to.
try: Unfollow one account today that only sells, and follow one that teaches for free.

title: Why should I not worship the One who made me?
subtitle: The simplest reason for faith
then: The man turns it into a personal question. Ibn Kathir paraphrases it: {idea}what is there to stop me from sincerely worshipping the One who created me?{/idea} He then reminds them that {trap}they too will return to Him for judgment.{/trap}
now: You find yourself needing a reason to pray today. {idea}Flip it around: why not?{/idea} The One who made your eyes, your hands, this morning, is asking for a few minutes.
old: I need a good reason to worship before I commit.
new: He made me. The real question is what is stopping me.
try: Before your next prayer, ask yourself this verse's question and answer it honestly.

title: If harm is meant for me, they could not save me.
subtitle: The helplessness of false gods
then: The man asks: {trap}shall I take other gods besides Him?{/trap} Ibn Kathir calls it a rebuke. These idols {trap}could neither harm nor benefit{/trap}, and if Allah willed harm, {idea}none could remove it but He.{/idea}
now: Lab results pending, you rely on the best clinic, the right connections, the insurance plan. {idea}They are means, not saviors.{/idea} {reward}The One who can remove harm is the One to ask first.{/reward}
old: With the right contacts and backup plans, I am covered.
new: Only Allah can remove harm. Everything else is just a means He may use.
try: Before your next appointment or big decision, ask Allah first, then use the means.

title: Then I would be clearly lost.
subtitle: Calling his own alternative by its name
then: He does not say you are in error. He says {idea}I would be in plain error{/idea} if I took them as gods. Ibn Kathir explains it means {trap}if I were to take them as gods instead of Allah.{/trap} He speaks of himself to soften their hearts.
now: When you want to correct someone, it is easy to say: you are wrong. {idea}This man said: if I did that, I would be wrong.{/idea} {reward}That is how you invite without attacking.{/reward}
old: Calling out other people's mistakes is the way to help them.
new: Speaking about myself first lets the truth reach others without a fight.
try: In your next disagreement, use an I sentence instead of a you sentence.

title: I have believed in your Lord, so hear me.
subtitle: Declaring faith openly, whatever it costs
then: Ibn Jarir thought he was speaking to the messengers: {idea}bear witness that I have believed.{/idea} The reports say his people then turned on him and killed him. Qatadah said {reward}he kept praying, O Allah, guide my people, for they do not know.{/reward}
now: Someone hurts you because of your faith, maybe a cruel comment from a coworker. {trap}You want to hit back.{/trap} {reward}This man, as he was being killed, prayed for his own people to be guided.{/reward}
old: When people hurt me for my faith, I have the right to hate them.
new: I can hold to my faith openly and still wish guidance for those who hurt me.
try: Make dua today for guidance for someone who has been unkind to you.

title: Enter Paradise. And his first thought was his people.
subtitle: Even after they killed him, he wished them good
then: After his people killed him, he was told: enter Paradise. Ibn Kathir says Allah {reward}took away all the sickness, grief, and exhaustion of this world.{/reward} Ibn Abbas said {idea}he was sincere to his people in life and after death.{/idea}
now: Someone in your life has hurt you badly. You imagine the day they finally get what they deserve. {idea}This man, the moment he reached Paradise, wished his killers could see it so they would be saved.{/idea}
old: Those who wronged me deserve to suffer.
new: A sincere heart wants guidance even for those who hurt it.
try: Say one dua today for the guidance of someone who wronged you.

title: My Lord forgave me and placed me among the honored.
subtitle: What he wished his people could see
then: Abu Mijlaz said he was forgiven {idea}because of his faith in his Lord and his belief in the messengers.{/idea} He wished his people could see {reward}the great reward and lasting blessings{/reward}, so they too would follow. Ibn Kathir: he was so keen for them to be guided.
now: You feel invisible at work, overlooked at family events, never the one people call important. {reward}This man was a sick rope worker from the edge of town.{/reward} {idea}Allah placed him among the honored.{/idea}
old: Being honored means being noticed by people.
new: True honor is being forgiven and honored by Allah, whoever notices me here.
try: Do one quiet act of faith today and remind yourself that Allah's honor is enough.

title: No army from the sky was needed.
subtitle: The matter was simpler than that for Allah
then: Ibn Masud, as Ibn Ishaq reported, said {idea}We did not seek to outnumber them, for the matter was simpler than that.{/idea} The town felt powerful after killing a believer. {trap}Its power counted for nothing.{/trap}
now: The bully at school, the manager who seems untouchable, the person who always gets away with it. {trap}They look so strong.{/trap} {idea}To Allah, no effort is needed at all.{/idea} You do not have to be the one who brings them down.
old: Some people are too powerful for anything to touch them.
new: No one is strong before Allah. He needs no army to deal with them.
try: Hand over one injustice that is eating at you to Allah in dua today, and let it rest.

title: One shout, and they were still.
subtitle: How quickly a proud town ended
then: Ibn Kathir reports that {trap}one blast came and they were all still{/trap}, leaving no trace. The word used is like a fire going out. The town that seemed so loud and sure of itself was silent in one moment.
now: You plan the next five years: the promotion, the house, the trip. {trap}All of it rests on breaths you do not control.{/trap} {idea}This is not to scare you but to wake you.{/idea} Live as someone who might be called any moment.
old: I have plenty of time before anything changes.
new: Everything can end in one moment. That makes today precious, not scary.
try: Settle one thing today you would not want left undone: an apology, a debt, a call.

title: What a regret for people: every messenger was mocked.
subtitle: Alas for those who neglected Allah's command
then: Qatadah said it means {trap}alas for mankind, who have neglected the command of Allah.{/trap} Ibn Kathir says they will feel this regret on the Day when they see what they denied. {trap}Every messenger was met with mockery.{/trap}
now: A meme about prayer, a joke about the hereafter in the group chat. You laugh along because everyone does. {trap}Mockery is the easiest way to dodge the truth.{/trap} {idea}Do not let a joke carry you past something serious.{/idea}
old: Joking about religion is harmless fun.
new: Mocking the message is how people have always avoided it, and it ends in regret.
try: The next time a joke mocks faith, do not forward it or laugh along.

title: So many generations gone, and none came back.
subtitle: One life here, no return
then: Ibn Kathir says those destroyed before {idea}came to this world only once and will not return to it.{/idea} He notes the verse refutes the belief that people {trap}come back to this world as they had been before.{/trap}
now: You walk through a graveyard, or scroll past old family photos. {idea}Every face there had one life, just like you.{/idea} {reward}You are in yours now, and it still has pages to fill.{/reward}
old: Somehow I will get another chance if I mess this up.
new: I have one life in this world. It is the only one, so it matters.
try: Visit or picture a graveyard this week and make dua for those resting there.

title: All of them will be brought before Us.
subtitle: Every nation, past and future, gathered
then: Ibn Kathir says {idea}all past nations and those yet to come will be gathered and brought to account{/idea} before Allah, and repaid for their good and evil deeds. He links it to the verse that {reward}your Lord will repay their works in full.{/reward}
now: At a packed stadium you feel like one face in sixty thousand. {idea}On that Day, you will not be lost in the crowd.{/idea} {reward}Every good thing you did will be found too.{/reward}
old: I am just one of billions. Nobody will notice my small deeds.
new: Every single person will stand before Allah, and every deed will be counted.
try: Do one deed today you would be glad to see on that Day.

title: The dead earth comes back to life and feeds you.
subtitle: A sign of the Creator and the Resurrection
then: Ibn Kathir says this is {idea}evidence of the Creator and His power to resurrect the dead.{/idea} The earth is dead and bare, then water comes and it swells with growth. {reward}It becomes provision for them and their cattle.{/reward}
now: You tear open a loaf of bread at breakfast without a thought. {idea}It started as a dry field that came back to life.{/idea} {reward}Every slice is a small sign of resurrection, and a gift.{/reward}
old: Food comes from the supermarket.
new: Food comes from dead earth brought to life, a sign of Allah's power and care.
try: Before your next meal, remember the field it came from and say alhamdulillah.

title: Gardens of dates and grapes, and springs bursting out.
subtitle: Variety and water placed where they are needed
then: For people in a dry land, gardens and springs were the clearest blessing. Ibn Kathir says Allah {reward}created rivers which flow to the places where they are needed{/reward}, and when reminding of blessings {idea}He mentions different kinds of fruit.{/idea}
now: You stand in the fruit aisle choosing between three kinds of grapes and complain the dates are pricey. {reward}Each one grew from water He sent to the right place.{/reward} {idea}Notice the gift before the price.{/idea}
old: Fruit and water are ordinary things.
new: Every fruit and every spring was placed for me by Allah, on purpose.
try: Eat one date or piece of fruit slowly today and thank Allah for it.

title: Your hands did not make it. Will you not be thankful?
subtitle: The fruit is His, even when you planted
then: Ibn Abbas and Qatadah said {idea}it all came by the mercy of Allah, not by their own labor and strength.{/idea} Ibn Jarir read it as including what their hands planted. Either way, the verse ends: {reward}will they not then give thanks?{/reward}
now: You finally get the raise, the good grade, the garden tomatoes. {trap}You think: I earned this.{/trap} {idea}You did the work, but the growth was His.{/idea} The verse just asks for thanks.
old: What I worked for is mine, I made it happen.
new: My effort was the means. The result was Allah's gift, and it deserves thanks.
try: Thank Allah out loud today for one result you have been calling your own achievement.

title: Glory to Him who made everything in pairs.
subtitle: Plants, people, and what we do not know
then: After listing gifts of the earth, the verse turns to praise. Ibn Kathir explains pairs as crops and plants, {idea}male and female among people{/idea}, and {idea}kinds of creatures they know nothing of.{/idea} He links it to: of everything We created pairs.
now: A documentary shows a new deep-sea creature no one had seen before. {idea}This verse already said there is more we do not know.{/idea} {reward}Every discovery is another reason to say subhanallah.{/reward}
old: Humans have pretty much figured out the natural world.
new: Creation is far larger than my knowledge, and all of it praises its Maker.
try: Say subhanallah 33 times today while thinking about something in nature that amazes you.

title: The day is peeled off the night, and darkness comes.
subtitle: Night as a sign
then: Ibn Kathir says Allah {idea}causes night and day to follow one another{/idea}, one coming as the other goes. The word used is like peeling off a skin. The Prophet ﷺ said when night comes and the sun sets, {reward}the fasting person breaks the fast.{/reward}
now: Sunset hits while you are still on a work call, lights coming on across the city. {idea}The day was just peeled off and you barely looked up.{/idea} Ramadan teaches you to watch this moment. Every day offers it.
old: Night just happens. It is the end of my productive hours.
new: Each nightfall is a sign of the One who peels the day away on time.
try: Stop for one minute at sunset today, look outside, and say subhanallah.

title: The sun runs toward its resting place by His decree.
subtitle: The decree of the Mighty, the Knowing
then: The Prophet ﷺ told Abu Dharr at sunset that {idea}the sun goes and prostrates beneath the Throne{/idea}, reciting this verse. Another view, Ibn Kathir notes, is that its term ends on the Day of Resurrection. {idea}It is the decree of the Almighty, the All-Knowing.{/idea}
now: Your weather app tells you sunrise at 6:42 tomorrow, to the minute. {idea}That precision is a decree, not an accident.{/idea} {reward}The sun bows to its Lord. You can too.{/reward}
old: The sun's movement is just physics, nothing to do with me.
new: The sun moves by Allah's decree and submits to Him. It invites me to submit as well.
try: Pray your next prayer on time today, matching the sun's own obedience.

title: The moon thins back into an old curved date stalk.
subtitle: Phases measured out for counting time
then: Ibn Kathir says Allah gave the moon {idea}an orbit from which the passing of months can be known.{/idea} It begins small, grows until {reward}full on the fourteenth night{/reward}, then wanes until it looks like the old dried, curved stalk of a date cluster.
now: You see the thin crescent from the car and someone says, Ramadan is near. {idea}The sky is a calendar Allah hung for everyone, free.{/idea} {trap}Full one week, thin the next, like every season of your life.{/trap}
old: The moon is just something nice to look at sometimes.
new: The moon's phases are a measured sign, marking my time and reminding me it passes.
try: Look for the moon tonight and notice which phase it is in. Say subhanallah.

title: Each swims in its own orbit, never colliding.
subtitle: Sun, moon, night, and day kept in their lanes
then: Ibn Kathir explains that Allah gave the sun its own light and the moon its own, and {idea}gave each its own orbit.{/idea} The sun dominates the day and the moon passes through phases. {idea}Neither overtakes the other.{/idea}
now: You fight to fit work, family, and prayer into one day, everything crashing into each other. {idea}The sky runs on lanes.{/idea} {reward}The same Lord can bring order to your days if you give each thing its place.{/reward}
old: My life is chaos, and that is just how it is.
new: The One who keeps every orbit in order can help me put my day in order.
try: Tomorrow, schedule your five prayers first, then fit the rest of your plans around them.

title: We carried your ancestors in the laden ship.
subtitle: The ark of Nuh as a sign
then: Ibn Kathir says the most significant ship is {idea}the ship of Nuh, in which Allah saved him and the believers.{/idea} Ibn Abbas said laden means filled. It carried luggage and animals, {reward}two of every kind.{/reward}
now: You trace your family tree on an app and feel proud of the names. {idea}Somewhere back there is a ship that Allah kept afloat.{/idea} {reward}Your life rests on an ancient rescue.{/reward}
old: My existence is just a long chain of biology.
new: I am here because Allah carried my ancestors to safety. My life is a mercy.
try: Make dua today for your parents and grandparents, living or passed.

title: And He made others like it for you to ride.
subtitle: Ships and camels as gifts of travel
then: Ibn Abbas gave two meanings. One: {reward}the camel, ship of the land{/reward}, which carries goods and riders. Another, held by many: {idea}the ships made after Nuh's ship, which was similar to it.{/idea}
now: You tap your phone and a car arrives, or you board a plane and sleep through a sea crossing. {idea}The materials, the minds, the physics: all created.{/idea} {reward}Every ride is a gift.{/reward}
old: Cars and planes are just human achievements.
new: Every ride I take is something Allah created for me, through people He taught.
try: Say the travel dua next time you get in a car or bus today.

title: If He willed, no one would hear the cry.
subtitle: Safety at sea is in His hands
then: Ibn Kathir says this refers to those on board ships: {trap}if He willed, there would be no one to save them from their predicament.{/trap} The verse reminds sea traders that {idea}their safety was never in their own hands.{/idea}
now: Turbulence over the ocean, the seatbelt sign pings, and suddenly you are praying. {idea}You were always that dependent, even on the calm flights.{/idea} {reward}Remember Him in the calm too.{/reward}
old: Modern safety systems mean I am fully protected.
new: Every safe journey is because Allah willed it. I depend on Him even when it is calm.
try: Next time you arrive somewhere safely, say alhamdulillah before you step out.

title: Saved only by mercy, enjoying it for a while.
subtitle: Every safe arrival has an end date
then: Ibn Kathir says Allah, {reward}by His mercy, makes it easy to travel on land and sea{/reward} and keeps people safe until an appointed time. The enjoyment lasts {idea}until a time known to Allah.{/idea}
now: Another normal day: you got home, ate, scrolled, slept. {reward}Each of those was mercy.{/reward} {idea}It is for a while, not forever.{/idea} Enjoy it with thanks and use it well.
old: Safe days are just normal. They are owed to me.
new: Each safe day is mercy lent for a while. It deserves thanks and good use.
try: Tonight before sleeping, thank Allah for keeping you safe today.

title: Beware what is before you and behind you.
subtitle: A call to mercy that went unanswered
then: Ibn Kathir says the idolaters {trap}ignored the sins they had committed and what was to come on the Day.{/trap} Mujahid said it refers to sins. If they had heeded it, {reward}Allah would have had mercy on them.{/reward} The wording implies they turned away.
now: You live in the moment, as the posters say. {trap}Old wrongs you never fixed. A future you never prepare for.{/trap} {idea}The verse asks you to glance back and look ahead, then you reach mercy.{/idea}
old: Looking back or worrying ahead is pointless. Just live now.
new: Repairing my past and preparing for my future is the path to mercy.
try: Seek forgiveness for one past sin and do one deed for your future today.

title: Every sign that came, they turned away from.
subtitle: Signs only help those who turn toward them
then: Ibn Kathir says signs of Allah's oneness and the truth of His messengers came to them, but {trap}they did not accept them or benefit from them.{/trap} The issue was not the signs. {idea}It was the turning away.{/idea}
now: This card has already shown you rain, fruit, the sun, the moon, a ship. {idea}Each was a sign.{/idea} {trap}You can scroll past all of them.{/trap} Or you can stop on one.
old: If a real sign came, I would definitely notice it.
new: Signs come all the time. What matters is whether I turn toward them or away.
try: Pick one sign from this surah and think about it for two minutes today.

title: Why feed them if Allah could feed them Himself?
subtitle: Using fate as an excuse not to give
then: When told to spend on the poor believers, they said {trap}if Allah wanted, He would have made them independent.{/trap} Ibn Kathir explains they claimed to be acting in line with Allah's will. {idea}They used fate as an excuse to keep their money.{/idea}
now: A man asks for help outside the station, and the thought comes: it is not my problem, someone else will sort it. {trap}That thought wears religious clothes sometimes.{/trap} {idea}Maybe you are the one Allah sent to feed him.{/idea}
old: Other people's needs are between them and Allah, not me.
new: Allah provides for people through people. I can be the means He uses.
try: Give food or a small amount of money to someone in need today.

title: So when is this promise, if you are telling the truth?
subtitle: Mocking the Day by demanding a date
then: Ibn Kathir says the disbelievers {trap}thought the Day of Resurrection would never come{/trap}, so they demanded a date to mock it. He links it to the verse that {trap}those who do not believe seek to hasten it.{/trap}
now: Someone at the table says: people have been saying the end is near for centuries. Everyone laughs. {idea}The date is not your business.{/idea} {reward}Your readiness is.{/reward}
old: If no one can tell me when, maybe it is not coming.
new: Not knowing the time is a reason to be ready always, not to doubt.
try: Ask yourself honestly tonight: if it came tomorrow, what would I wish I had done today?

title: One blast, while they are busy arguing.
subtitle: The Hour comes in the middle of ordinary life
then: Ibn Kathir explains the blast as the Trumpet sounded {trap}while people are in their marketplaces and workplaces, arguing as they usually do.{/trap} Everyone will tilt their head to listen. {idea}It interrupts ordinary life.{/idea}
now: You are mid-argument with your spouse about the dishes, or haggling on the phone with a supplier. {trap}That is exactly where people will be.{/trap} {idea}Is this argument worth being in when it comes?{/idea}
old: There will be some sign before the end, so I can prepare later.
new: The Hour will come in the middle of normal life. Normal life is where I prepare.
try: End one argument today early, with a kind word, instead of winning it.

title: No time to leave instructions, no way to get home.
subtitle: What cannot be done once it begins
then: Ibn Kathir says they {trap}will not be able to make a bequest about their possessions{/trap}, for the matter will be far more serious, nor go back to their families. {idea}Whatever needed saying had to be said before.{/idea}
now: You have been meaning to tell your mother you are grateful. To repay that loan. To make peace with your brother. {trap}You assume there will be a goodbye.{/trap} {reward}Say it now, while you can still go home.{/reward}
old: There will be time to say what matters before the end.
new: There may be no last moment. What matters should be said and done now.
try: Tell one family member today something you have been meaning to say to them.

title: One blast, and everyone is walking toward their Lord.
subtitle: The rising from the graves
then: Ibn Kathir explains this is the blast of resurrection, when people come out of their graves. {idea}Yansilun{/idea} means they walk quickly. The Quraysh who heard it mocked the idea of rising again, and this verse simply describes it happening.
now: You drive past a cemetery on the way to work and do not even look. Rows of names, dates, flowers going dry. {idea}Every one of those stones will open.{/idea} And one day someone will drive past yours.
old: Death is a full stop and the grave is where the story ends.
new: The grave is a waiting room, and the road out of it leads straight to my Lord.
try: Next time you pass a grave or a cemetery, slow down and make a short dua for the people in it.

title: Who woke us up? The promise did.
subtitle: Waking up to what was always promised
then: Ibn Kathir says the grave will feel like a {trap}short nap{/trap} next to what comes after. Waking, the deniers ask who raised them. The reply, from the believers or the angels, is that {idea}this is what the Most Merciful promised.{/idea}
now: The alarm goes off and for a second you do not know where you are. Then it all comes back: the meeting, the deadline, the thing you put off. {trap}You knew it was coming.{/trap} The verse asks you to remember that feeling before the real waking.
old: If it were really true, someone would have warned me properly.
new: I have been told, clearly and kindly, and the Merciful keeps His word.
try: Think of one reminder you keep snoozing. Act on a small part of it today.

title: It takes one shout to gather everyone who ever lived.
subtitle: How easy the gathering is for Allah

row.title: one command
sub: like a blink of an eye

then: Ibn Kathir links this to verses saying the Hour comes {idea}like the twinkling of an eye.{/idea} The listeners thought raising scattered bones was impossible. Allah answers: {idea}one command, and all are present.{/idea}
now: Getting your whole family in one room for a wedding photo takes weeks of planning and still someone is late. Now picture every human being, standing together, with no one missing. {idea}One word is enough for Him.{/idea}
old: Bringing everyone back sounds too big to be real.
new: What is huge for me is a single word for Allah.
try: When something feels impossible today, say: it is easy for Allah. Then do your part.

title: No one is wronged. You get exactly what you did.
subtitle: Perfect fairness on that Day
then: Ibn Kathir says this means no one will be wronged regarding their deeds. After describing the gathering, the verse settles the question of justice: {idea}nothing counted that you did not do.{/idea}
now: At work someone else takes credit for your project. In the family your effort goes unseen. It stings. {reward}On that Day nothing you did is lost{/reward}, and {trap}nothing you did is hidden either.{/trap}
old: Life is unfair, and no one will ever see what I really put in.
new: Every deed is counted exactly, so mine are worth guarding.
try: Do one good thing today that nobody will see or thank you for.

title: In Paradise, people are busy, and the busyness is joy.
subtitle: A full life with no stress in it
then: Ibn Kathir says the people of Paradise will be {reward}too occupied with their delights{/reward} to think of anything else. Mujahid and Qatadah said busy with what they enjoy. Ibn Abbas said it means rejoicing.
now: Your days are full: school runs, shifts, messages piling up, a to-do list that never ends. Busy usually means tired. {reward}Here is a busy that only fills you up.{/reward} The tiredness of now is not the last word.
old: Being busy always means being drained.
new: There is a fullness waiting that is pure joy, and today's effort walks toward it.
try: Pick one task you do today and do it for Allah's sake, so the busyness counts.

title: Together with their spouses, in shade, at rest.
subtitle: Rest that is shared, not lonely
then: Mujahid said the shade is the shade of trees. Many early scholars said the couches are {reward}beds beneath canopies.{/reward} For people in the hot sun of Makkah, shade and rest with family was a picture they knew well.
now: You and your spouse sit on the same sofa at night, each lost in a separate screen. Tired, close, but not really together. {reward}The verse shows rest that is shared.{/reward} A little of that is possible now.
old: Rest means getting away from everyone.
new: The best rest is with the people I love, in ease and calm.
try: Spend ten minutes tonight with someone at home, phones away, just talking.

title: Fruit, and whatever they ask for.
subtitle: Wishes that are finally answered

key.label: The gap between want and have

then: Ibn Kathir says the fruit is {reward}of all kinds{/reward}, and whatever they ask for they will find. In dry Makkah, fresh fruit was a luxury. The listeners heard of a place with no wish left unmet.
now: Your cart has three things in it you do not need. Payday comes and the money is gone by the weekend. {trap}The wanting never stops here.{/trap} {reward}There, asking and having are the same thing.{/reward}
old: If I just get this next thing, I will be satisfied.
new: Full satisfaction is real, but it lives in Paradise, not in my cart.
try: Remove one item from a wish list or cart today, and ask Allah for Paradise instead.

title: Peace, spoken to you by your Merciful Lord.
subtitle: The greeting above every other gift
then: Ibn Abbas said that Allah, {idea}Who is As-Salam{/idea}, will Himself greet the people of Paradise with peace. Ibn Kathir links it to the verse: their greeting on the Day they meet Him will be {reward}Salam.{/reward}
now: You remember the day a parent or a teacher said, I am proud of you. Years later, it still warms you. Now imagine the Lord of everything saying {reward}peace{/reward} to you, by name.
old: Paradise is mostly about getting nice things.
new: The sweetest part is being spoken to with peace by my Lord.
try: Say salam with full meaning to three people today, looking at them.

title: Stand apart today, you who chose wrong.
subtitle: The day the crowd is divided
then: Ibn Kathir says the disbelievers will be commanded to {trap}stand apart from the believers.{/trap} He links it to verses saying people will be divided into two groups on that Day. In Makkah, deniers and believers lived side by side, often in the same family.
now: In the office everyone pads their hours a bit, so it feels fine. In the group chat everyone laughs at the cruel joke, so you do too. {idea}That Day, nobody stands behind everybody.{/idea}
old: If everyone around me does it, it cannot be that bad.
new: I will stand on my own deeds, not on what the crowd did.
try: Notice one thing you do only because others do it. Skip it once today.

title: You were told: do not obey your clear enemy.
subtitle: The old warning about Shaytan
then: Ibn Kathir calls this {trap}a rebuke{/trap} to those who obeyed Shaytan although he was a plain enemy, and disobeyed the Most Merciful {reward}Who created them and gave them provision.{/reward}
now: It is late and a voice in your head says: just one more video, skip the prayer, you can make it up. It sounds like a friend. {trap}It is not.{/trap} The verse names who is really talking.
old: That urge is just me being tired.
new: Some urges come from an enemy, and I was told to recognise him.
try: When a bad nudge comes today, say a'udhu billahi min ash-shaytan ar-rajim, then wait a moment.

title: Worship Me. That is the straight road.
subtitle: The simple path that was offered
then: Ibn Kathir explains Allah is saying: {idea}I commanded you to worship Me{/idea}, and that is the straight path, but {trap}you followed a different path.{/trap} The Quraysh were being asked to drop their idols and turn to one Lord.
now: You keep looking for the right method, the perfect routine, the productivity app that will finally fix your life. {idea}The straight path is not complicated.{/idea} It is turning to Allah, then again, then again.
old: Finding the right way to live is confusing and hard.
new: The way is straight: worship Allah, and come back each time I drift.
try: Pray your next prayer on time, and treat it as one step on the straight road.

title: He misled huge crowds. Did you not think?
subtitle: Numbers are not proof of the right way
then: Mujahid, Qatadah and others said it means {trap}a large number of people.{/trap} Ibn Kathir explains the question: did you not have understanding, when you left worshipping your Lord alone and {trap}preferred to follow Shaytan?{/trap}
now: A trend has millions of views, so it must be fine. Everyone at work does it this way, so it must be right. {idea}A big crowd going one way is not a reason.{/idea} The verse hands you back your own mind.
old: If so many people do it, it is probably fine.
new: Crowds have been misled before, so I am meant to think for myself.
try: Before you follow one trend or habit today, ask: would I choose this if no one else did?

title: This is the very thing you were warned about.
subtitle: When a warning becomes real
then: Ibn Kathir says this is said after Hell is shown to them: {trap}this is what the messengers warned you about{/trap}, and you did not believe them. The Quraysh had heard the warning many times and laughed it off.
now: The doctor said cut down on sugar. The bank sent three letters. You meant to deal with it. {idea}A warning is a gift while there is still time to act on it.{/idea} Today there is still time.
old: Warnings are exaggerated to scare people.
new: Every warning I hear now is mercy, because it comes before it is too late.
try: Think of one warning in your life you have ignored, about faith or health, and take one step on it.

title: The result follows what you kept denying.
subtitle: Consequence tied to a lifelong choice
then: Ibn Kathir explains the reason is given in the verse itself: {trap}because you used to disbelieve.{/trap} The words "used to" point to a habit kept up over a life, not a single slip.
now: No one becomes a different person in one day. It is the small yes and no, repeated: the prayer delayed again, the lie told again. {idea}Habits become a direction.{/idea} {reward}So do good habits.{/reward}
old: One choice here or there does not really shape where I end up.
new: What I keep doing becomes who I am, so I can choose my habits on purpose.
try: Pick one small good habit and do it today, even for two minutes.

title: Mouths sealed. Hands and feet tell the truth.
subtitle: When your own body is the witness

row.title: I can talk my way out

then: Ibn Kathir says this is for those who {trap}deny their sins and swear they did not do them.{/trap} He cites a hadith in Muslim where a servant asks for a witness only from himself, and {trap}his own limbs speak.{/trap}
now: Your hands typed that message. Your feet walked to that place. Your eyes scrolled past that page. You can delete the history on your phone. {idea}Your hands keep their own record.{/idea}
old: If no one saw and I deny it, it is gone.
new: My own body is a witness, so I want to give it good things to tell.
try: Look at your hands today and ask: what will they say about this day? Do one thing they can be proud of.

title: Sight itself is a gift He could take away.
subtitle: Seeing the path is not your own doing
then: Ibn Abbas explained it two ways: Allah could have {trap}blinded them{/trap}, or misguided them from the truth. Mujahid and others said they would struggle to find the right way. {idea}Their sight was a mercy they took for granted.{/idea}
now: You read this on a screen without thinking about it. You find your way through traffic, read a child's face, know right from wrong. {reward}All of that is sight being given to you right now.{/reward}
old: Seeing clearly, with my eyes or my heart, is just normal.
new: Every clear sight I have is something Allah is giving, not something I own.
try: Close your eyes for ten seconds, then open them and say alhamdulillah for sight.

title: Stuck in place, unable to go forward or back.
subtitle: Being able to move is also a gift

row.title: movement is a gift
sub: use it while you have it

then: Scholars gave different meanings: Ibn Abbas said destroyed, As-Suddi said their form changed, Abu Salih said {trap}turned to stone.{/trap} Ibn Kathir sums it up: they would {trap}remain static{/trap}, unable to move forwards or backwards.
now: You keep saying you will change next month: start praying properly, call your mother, quit the habit. You assume you will always be free to move. {reward}Right now you can still step forward.{/reward}
old: I can always turn around later.
new: The ability to change is itself a gift, and today I still have it.
try: Take one step today on a change you keep postponing.

title: Live long enough and strength turns back to weakness.
subtitle: Ageing as a sign this world ends
then: Ibn Kathir says the longer a person lives, {trap}the weaker he becomes after being strong.{/trap} He links it to 30:54. The lesson: this world is passing, so people should realise {idea}they were created for another world{/idea} that will not pass away.
now: You visit your grandmother and she asks your name twice. You notice your own back hurts when you get out of bed. {idea}The body is quietly telling you this place is temporary.{/idea}
old: Getting old is just a sad thing that happens.
new: Ageing is a reminder that I was made for something that lasts.
try: Visit or call an elderly relative today and listen to them for a while.

title: Not poetry. A reminder, and a clear Quran.
subtitle: Why the Quran is not just beautiful words
then: Some of the Quraysh called the Quran {trap}poetry{/trap}, or magic. Ibn Kathir says Allah did not teach the Prophet ﷺ poetry, and he had no inclination toward it. The Quran is {idea}a reminder, clear to the one who ponders.{/idea}
now: You play a beautiful recitation in the car and it feels peaceful. That is good. But {idea}it is also talking to you{/idea}, about your choices this week. The sound is the door, not the room.
old: The Quran is beautiful to listen to.
new: The Quran is beautiful, and it is also a clear message meant for me.
try: Next time you hear a recitation, look up the meaning of just one verse you heard.

title: It warns whoever is alive inside.
subtitle: A living heart is what hears it
then: Ibn Kathir says the Quran warns every living person. Those who benefit are, as Qatadah said, {reward}alive of heart and alive of insight.{/reward} It is {reward}a mercy to believers{/reward} and evidence against those who reject it.
now: You can sit through a reminder at Friday prayer and feel nothing, thinking about lunch. Some days the heart is numb. {idea}The verse asks you to keep it alive{/idea}, so the words can land.
old: If a reminder does not move me, it is not for me.
new: When a reminder does not move me, my heart needs reviving, and I can work on that.
try: Read one short passage of Quran slowly today, and ask Allah to keep your heart alive.

title: Cattle made by Him, and you call yourself their owner.
subtitle: Ownership that is really a gift

row.title: I was given it
sub: He made it, then handed it over

then: Ibn Kathir calls this a {reward}sign and a blessing{/reward}. Qatadah said they are their masters. For desert Arabs, camels were wealth, transport and food. The verse asks them to {idea}see who made what they owned.{/idea}
now: Your car, your flat, the phone in your hand. You saved for it, so it feels like yours. {idea}Every material it is made of, He made first.{/idea} Your name is on the receipt, not on the creation.
old: I worked for it, so it is simply mine.
new: What I own was made by Allah and placed in my hands.
try: Pick one thing you own and use often. Say alhamdulillah for it before you use it today.

title: A child can lead a camel because He tamed it.
subtitle: Strong things made gentle for you

row.title: His subduing
sub: He made it submit to me

then: Ibn Kathir notes that a large camel submits so easily that {idea}even a young child{/idea} can make it kneel and lead it, even a whole train of a hundred camels. That ease is {reward}a blessing from Allah{/reward}, not human strength.
now: You get into a two-tonne car and it goes where you steer. Electricity, water from a tap, a plane in the sky. {reward}Huge forces, made gentle enough for you.{/reward} You only notice when they stop working.
old: I am in control of the things I use.
new: Allah made these strong things easy for me, and that ease is a gift.
try: Next time you start the car or turn on a tap, say subhanalladhi sakhkhara lana hadha.

title: Wool, milk, comfort. Will they not be grateful?
subtitle: The question after a list of gifts
then: Ibn Kathir lists the benefits: {reward}wool, fur, hair, furnishings{/reward}, and milk to drink. The question at the end asks: will they not {idea}worship the Creator of all this{/idea}, instead of thanking others?
now: Your jumper, the milk in your tea, the leather on your shoes. You thank the waiter, the delivery driver, maybe your own hard work. {idea}The verse asks you to look one step further back.{/idea}
old: I am grateful to the people who bring me things.
new: Behind every gift and every giver is Allah, and He deserves the first thanks.
try: At your next meal or cup of tea, pause and thank Allah by name before the first sip.

title: They took other gods, hoping to be helped.
subtitle: Looking for help in the wrong place
then: Ibn Kathir says the idolators hoped their gods would {trap}help them, provide for them, and bring them closer to Allah.{/trap} The Quraysh kept idols around the Kabah for exactly this reason.
now: Things get hard and you reach for something: a person you think can fix it, a lucky charm, a contact, money in the bank. {trap}You turn to it before you turn to Allah.{/trap} The verse asks where your hope goes first.
old: If I have the right connections, I will be fine.
new: Help comes from Allah first, and everything else is only a means.
try: Next time you need help today, make a short dua before you call or message anyone.

title: They cannot help you, yet you defend them like soldiers.
subtitle: Fighting for things that cannot fight for you
then: Qatadah said the idolators {trap}used to get angry for the sake of their gods{/trap}, but the gods could not benefit or protect them. Mujahid said the idols will be present at the Reckoning, {trap}as proof against those who worshipped them.{/trap}
now: You argue online for a celebrity who does not know you exist. You defend a brand, a team, a habit, like it is family. {idea}All that loyalty, and it cannot help you on the day you need it.{/idea}
old: Standing up for the things I love shows I am loyal.
new: My loyalty belongs to what can truly help me, and that is Allah.
try: Notice one thing you get heated defending. Ask if it would ever stand up for you.

title: Do not let their words grieve you. We know.
subtitle: Comfort for the Prophet ﷺ when mocked
then: Ibn Kathir calls this {reward}consolation for the Mercy to the Worlds{/reward}. The Prophet ﷺ was hurt by their denial. Allah tells him: {idea}We know what they conceal and what they reveal{/idea}, and nothing will be overlooked.
now: Someone says something cruel about you in the family chat. You replay it at 2am, writing replies in your head. {idea}Allah heard it, and He knows what they meant.{/idea} You do not have to carry it alone.
old: I have to answer every hurtful word or it will stay with me.
new: Allah knows exactly what was said and why, so I can set it down.
try: Think of one hurtful comment you keep replaying. Hand it to Allah in a quiet dua and let it go.

title: Made from a drop, and now arguing with his Maker.
subtitle: Forgetting where you came from

row.title: look at yourself
sub: He made you from a drop

then: Early scholars said a man of Quraysh came to the Prophet ﷺ with {trap}a dry bone, crumbling it in the air{/trap}, asking if Allah would revive this. These closing verses came down. Ibn Kathir says they apply to {idea}everyone who denies the resurrection.{/idea}
now: You hold a newborn in a hospital corridor. A few months ago it did not exist. Twenty years later that same child may be arguing that nothing can come back. {idea}The proof is the person asking the question.{/idea}
old: Some things are just too hard to believe.
new: The One who made me from nothing can easily make me again.
try: Look at your hand for a moment and remember it started as a drop. Say subhanallah.

title: He asks who revives rotten bones, forgetting his own start.
subtitle: The objection that forgets itself
then: Ibn Kathir says the man thinks it unlikely that Allah will remake dry bones, and {trap}forgets that Allah created him from nothing.{/trap} Looking at himself, he can see something greater than what he denies.
now: You doubt you can change, recover, or start over. Yet you have already been through things you once thought would break you. {idea}You forget your own story.{/idea} Allah has brought you this far.
old: This is too far gone to be fixed.
new: Allah began me from nothing, so nothing is too far gone for Him.
try: Write down one hard thing Allah already brought you through. Read it when doubt comes.

title: The One who made them first will give them life.
subtitle: He knows where every bone went
then: Ibn Kathir says Allah knows the bones in every region of the earth, {idea}wherever they went when they scattered.{/idea} He cites a hadith of a man who had his ashes scattered out of fear; Allah gathered him and {reward}forgave him.{/reward}
now: You lose a ring in the sea, a photo from years ago, a friend's number. Gone forever. {idea}Nothing is lost to Allah{/idea}, not a bone, not a tear, not a good deed you forgot you did.
old: Once something is scattered or forgotten, it is gone.
new: Allah knows every part of His creation, and nothing slips from Him.
try: Remember one good deed you did long ago and forgot. Thank Allah that He did not forget.

title: Fire from a green tree. Life from the dead.
subtitle: Opposites coming out of each other

row.title: He brings one from another
sub: fire from green, life from dust

then: Ibn Abbas said this refers to trees of the Hijaz, the {idea}Markh and Afar{/idea}: rub two green branches together and fire comes out. Qatadah said the One who brings fire from this tree is {idea}able to resurrect.{/idea}
now: You flick a lighter or turn on the gas. The fuel came from plants that grew long ago, green and alive. {idea}Warmth from what was once a leaf.{/idea} Allah brings things out of their opposites all the time.
old: Something lifeless cannot come back to life.
new: Allah brings fire out of green wood, so He can bring life out of the dust.
try: When you next see a flame today, remember this verse and the resurrection.

title: He made the heavens and earth. You are the easy part.
subtitle: Measuring the resurrection against the universe
then: Ibn Kathir says Allah points to the {idea}seven heavens and seven earths{/idea} with everything in them, as proof He can re-create our bodies. He links it to 40:57: creating the heavens and earth is {idea}greater than creating people.{/idea}
now: You stand outside on a clear night far from the city lights and see more stars than you can count. Then you worry whether your small life can be put back together. {idea}Look up.{/idea}
old: My problems and my life feel too big to fix.
new: Next to the sky He built, my life is small and easy for Him.
try: Step outside tonight and look at the sky for one minute before bed.

title: He says Be, and it is.
subtitle: How Allah makes things happen
then: Ibn Kathir says He only needs to command a thing {idea}once{/idea}; it does not need repeating. He cites a hadith qudsi: {reward}My giving is a word{/reward}, and when I want a thing I say Be, and it is.
now: You have been praying for the same thing for months: a job, a child, a healing, a way out of debt. It feels huge. {reward}For Him it is one word.{/reward} The timing is His, and the ease is His too.
old: What I am asking for is too big or too complicated.
new: Nothing I ask is hard for Allah; He only says Be.
try: Make one dua today for the thing that feels most impossible, and ask with certainty.

title: Everything is in His hand, and you are going back to Him.
subtitle: The closing line of Ya-Sin
then: Ibn Kathir explains this as glorifying the One {idea}in Whose hand is control of the heavens and earth{/idea}, to Whom all return on the Day of Resurrection. He mentions the Prophet ﷺ praising {reward}the Owner of Malakut{/reward} in long night prayers.
now: You close your laptop at the end of a long day, worried about rent, the kids, your health. You think it is all on you. {idea}It is all in His hand.{/idea} And every road, including yours, goes home to Him.
old: Everything depends on me holding it together.
new: Everything is in Allah's hand, and I am on my way back to Him.
try: Before sleeping tonight, say subhanallah slowly a few times and hand Him the worries of the day.
